svg.aria-label: Amazon S3: object storage, not a disk. In your applications, servers, containers, and a Lambda function read and write a private S3 bucket over HTTPS. A browser asks your backend for a presigned URL, then downloads the object directly from the bucket. A CloudFront distribution serves the static website and reads the private bucket through origin access control. The bucket my-app-uploads holds objects, each one data plus metadata, named by keys whose prefixes, such as uploads/2026/11/, are not real folders. Storage classes Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, and Glacier set the price by how often you read, and versioning keeps previous versions for backups.
svg.title: Amazon S3: applications, browsers through presigned URLs, and CloudFront all reach one private bucket of objects
